{{Quote|Look at the Atrisi system, for example. The principal planet still recalls the Kitel Phard Dynasty with pride. These rulers unified the entire homeworld, eliminating opposition and establishing a golden age.|Major Arhul Hextrophon|<ref name="IS2" />}}
'''Atrisia''', also known as '''Kitel Phard''', was a terrestrial [[Planet/Legends|planet]] located in the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] [[Sector/Legends|sector]] known as the [[Atrisian Commonwealth/Legends|Atrisian Commonwealth]]. It lay on the [[Giju Run/Legends|Giju Run]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] and was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Species/Legends|creature]] known as the [[shredder bat]]. Locations on the planet included the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Jar'Kai (city)|Jar'Kai]] and the [[Atrisian Imperial Historical Library]].

Atrisia was inhabited by a race of [[Human/Legends|Humans]] known as the [[Atrisian]]s. During their homeworld's ancient history, the Atrisians had formed several nations, including the [[Atrisian Empire]], which actively engaged in conquests. Under the leadership of the fifty-forth [[Atrisian Emperor/Legends|Atrisian Emperor]], [[Uueg Tching]], the Empire's [[Kitel Phard Dynasty]] unified the planet, and Atrisia was subsequently also referred to as "Kitel Phard." Tching also [[Author/Legends|authored]] a collection of parables, analogies, and instructions known as the ''[[Sayings]]'', which began to circulate in the wider [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] [[Millennium/Legends|millennia]] later.

By [[24,500 BBY]], a type of [[Jar'Kai dueling saber|dueling sword]] and an associated [[Jar'Kai/Legends|dual-wielding sword-fighting technique]] was developed in the Atrisian city of Jar'Kai. At the conclusion of the [[First Great Schism]] around the same [[Time/Legends|time]], the [[Legions of Lettow]] member [[Arden Lyn]] traveled beyond Atrisia while fleeing the forces of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]].

Nearly [[539 BBY|twenty-four millennia]] later, the [[Atrisian Parliament]] took over power from the planet's [[Emperor/Legends|emperors]]. Atrisia subsequently became a part of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], by which time its ancient history was considered a classical field of [[Galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Historian/Legends|historical]] studies. The achievements of the Atrisian Empire served as an inspiration for the formation of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], of which the planet became a member. Atrisia also joined the Empire's successor, the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], and fell within the borders of [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire]] a [[137 ABY|century]] later.

==Description==
{{Quote|The predator known as the shredder bat was first encountered on the ancient planet of Atrisia; ''[&hellip;].''<nowiki />|Holobrochure for the Tagge Holographic Museum of Chandrila|<ref name="Creatures" />}}
Atrisia, also occasionally referred to as Kitel Phard,<ref name="TEA" /> was the principal<ref name="IS2" /> [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="TEA" /> of the [[Atrisi system]].<ref name="IS2" /> It was a part of the [[Atrisian Commonwealth/Legends|Atrisian Commonwealth]], a [[Sector/Legends|sector]] of [[Realspace/Legends|space]] in the [[Southern Core]] portion of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]].<ref name="TEA" />

The planet lay at the endpoint of the [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] known as the [[Giju Run/Legends|Giju Run]], which, after a short detour through the [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies]], connected Atrisia to the Core Worlds' [[Dahrtag system/Legends|Dahrtag system]].<ref name="TEA" /> Additionally, a set of [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] routes led beyond Atrisia, connecting it to a tangle of [[Star/Legends|stars]] and, ultimately, the astronomical object [[Irkalla]]<ref name="EGTW" /> in the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]].<ref name="EAOC Irkalla">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}} &mdash; Based on corresponding data for [[Irkalla system/Legends|Irkalla system]]</ref>

Atrisia was a terrestrial world with several continents on its surface.<ref name="IS2" /> The [[Diet/Legends|predatory]] [[Species/Legends|creature]] known as the [[shredder bat]] was first encountered on the planet but eventually spread to more than a thousand other worlds.<ref name="Creatures" />

==History==
===The Kitel Phard Dynasty===
{{Quote|Uueg increased the Atrisian Empire to rule, directly or indirectly, the whole of Kitel Phard.|Lecture by Doctor Corellia Antilles|<ref name="Files" />}}
Atrisia was [[Colonist/Legends|colonized]] by [[Human/Legends|Humans]].<ref name="TEA" /> The state known as the [[Atrisian Empire]], led by the [[First Atrisian Emperor]],<ref name="Written">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/source/writtenword/index.html?page=1|text=The Written Word|int=The Written Word}}</ref> was among several nations formed on the planet,<ref name="IS2" /> and the early [[Atrisian Emperor/Legends|rulers]] of that [[Emperor/Legends|empire]] carried out brutal conquests.<ref name="Written" /> [[Blood/Legends|Bloody]] wars ensued, with the [[Third Atrisian period]] being a particularly tumultuous [[Time/Legends|time]] in the planet's history.<ref name="Files" />

[[File:UuegTching-TEA.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Emperor Uueg Tching unified Atrisia.]]
The emperors of the [[Kitel Phard Dynasty]] subsequently carried out the process of eliminating any opposition and unifying Atrisia.<ref name="IS2" /> That unification was completed during the rule of the fifty-fourth Atrisian Emperor, [[Uueg Tching]].<ref name="Files" /> During his reign, Tching enjoyed successes against the nations inhabiting the recently discovered continents of the planet.<ref name="IS2" /> Upon his victory over the last of Atrisia's continents,<ref name="Written" /> Tching had expanded the Atrisian Empire to rule, directly or indirectly, over the entirety of his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]]<ref name="Files" /> and had also established planetwide use of the [[Writing/Legends|writing system]] known as the [[Atrisian script]].<ref name="Written" />

The fifty-fourth Emperor of Atrisia became famous for his tyrannical rule and his insight into strategy, [[Diplomat/Legends|diplomacy]], and the effective use of [[Spy/Legends|spies]]<ref name="CSWE Tching" /> and subverted more than thirty separate rebellions against his rule.<ref name="IS2" /> [[Atrisian]] court<ref name="Written" /> scribes hand-recorded the ''[[Sayings]]'', a collection of instructional parables, analogies, and advice that Tching [[Author/Legends|compiled]] as a guide for his successors.<ref name="Files" /> In time, Tching became a legendary ruler,<ref name="IS2" /> with the following [[Tching Dynasty]] being named after him,<ref name="Files" /> and later Atrisians remembered with pride<ref name="IS2" /> both him<ref name="Files" /> and the Kitel Phard Dynasty as a whole. The dynasty's actions ushered in a golden age,<ref name="IS2" /> and Atrisia was later occasionally referred to as "Kitel Phard" after those rulers.<ref name="TEA" />

===Planet of Twin Swords===
{{Quote|I fled into the tangled stars beyond Kitel Phard, following secret ways Xendor had discovered.|Arden Lyn|<ref name="EGTW" />}}
[[File:Jar-Kai_dueling_sabers.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Atrisia was the origin point of Jar'Kai dueling swords.]]
By [[24,500 BBY]],<ref name="Date Jar'Kai">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20050526a|series=The Dark Forces Saga|text=Part 4: Of the Crudest Matter}} establishes that the [[Jar'Kai/Legends|dual-wielding sword-fighting technique]] used by the [[Yovshin Swordsmen]] preceded that utilized by the [[Legions of Lettow]]. Since {{CSWECite|I|xi|A Timeline of Galactic Events}} dates both the formation and the defeat of the latter organization to [[24,500 BBY]], the former must have practiced their own [[Jar'Kai dueling saber|sword]]-fighting form by that [[Standard year/Legends|year]].</ref> pairs of specific [[Jar'Kai dueling saber|dueling swords]] were first crafted in the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Jar'Kai (city)|Jar'Kai]] on Atrisia. The [[Yovshin Swordsmen]] of the Atrisian Empire named those weapons after the settlement, and their [[Jar'Kai/Legends|dual-wielding sword-fighting technique]] using the paired [[Sword/Legends|blades]]<ref name="TDFS4" /> was also developed in the city.<ref name="CSWE Jar'Kai">{{CSWECite|II|140|Jar'Kai}}</ref> Around that same [[Standard year/Legends|year]],<ref name="Date Lettow">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' establishes that [[Xendor]] had discovered secret [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]] beyond Atrisia by the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[First Great Schism]], which the timeline presented in ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' dates to [[24,500 BBY]].</ref> [[Xendor]], the leader of the [[Legions of Lettow]], discovered a number of secret hyperlanes leading beyond Atrisia. When the [[First Great Schism]] concluded with the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] [[Battle of Lettow|attacking]] the Legions at [[Lettow]], several of the Legionnaires fled and left the borders of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. [[Arden Lyn]], the former lover of the [[Death/Legends|deceased]] Xendor, sought refuge in space beyond Atrisia but was eventually cornered by the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] on Irkalla.<ref name="EGTW" />

The Atrisians eventually left their homeworld, which became one of the approximately 200 settled worlds known as the Atrisian Commonwealth. The area of space surrounding Atrisia was [[Scout/Legends|explored]] by the Galactic Republic at some point between [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]] and [[3996 BBY]] and thus became part of what was considered the civilized [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]. Contact with the independent Atrisian Commonwealth led to the growth of the Southern Core, a region of the Core Worlds and the Colonies.<ref name="TEA" />

{{GameMechanics|legends=1|Star Wars: The Old Republic}}
By [[3643 BBY]],<ref name="Date TOR">Per the reasoning [[Template:TOR_dates|here]], Act I of ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' takes place around [[3643 BBY]]. Since players of ''The Old Republic'' can assign their companions on the mission "Sword Fodder" independently of the main class storyline at any point during the game, the mission must take place at some point around 3643 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]].</ref> weapon masters on Atrisia intended to test their students by having them face battle-hardened fighters, the latter of which the masters found themselves in need. An individual subsequently dispatched a companion to recruit skilled warriors who were up to the task posed by the Atrisian weaponsmiths. The companion discovered a group of captured warriors affiliated with the<ref name="Sword Fodder">{{TORcite|type=crewskill|Underworld Trading|Sword Fodder}}</ref> ancient [[Morgukai]] order<ref name="CSWE Morgukai">{{CSWECite|II|331|Morgukai Warriors}}</ref> and delivered them to [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]],<ref name="Sword Fodder" /> an [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] planet<ref name="TEA" /> housing the [[Sith Academy (Korriban)|Sith Academy]] of the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted Sith Empire]].<ref name="Holonet Korriban">{{Holonet|planets|korriban|Korriban}}</ref> No more than [[3638 BBY|five years]] later,<ref name="Date RotHC">{{TORweb|url=community/showthread.php?p=9852711#edit9852711|text=Charles Boyd on Forums: "Dear Story Team, What Year Are We Currently In?" (1)}} &mdash; According to ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''{{'s}} lead designer, [[Charles Boyd]], the events of the digital expansion [[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Rise of the Hutt Cartel|''Rise of the Hutt Cartel'']] take place in [[3638 BBY]]. The Crew Skill mission "Swords of Atrisia" is part of the ''Rise of the Hutt Cartel'' expansion and therefore also takes place in that [[Standard year/Legends|year]].</ref> a [[Unidentified treasure hunter|treasure hunter]] claimed to have discovered Jar'Kai swords belonging to one of the first Yovshin Swordsmen. An interested party then sent a companion to confirm that the find was genuine.<ref name="Swords of Atrisia">{{TORcite|exp=rothc|type=crewskill|Archaeology|Swords of Atrisia}}</ref>
{{Endgame}}

===The Parliament and the Republic===
{{Quote|After spending over two millennia available only to the nobility, the Parliament showed the authority it had finally wrested from the throne by reproducing the ''Sayings'' in both a database format and special printed edition. Now widely available, the ''Sayings'' began making their way off of the planet.|Doctor Milanda Vorgan, "The Written Word: A Brief Introduction to the Writing Systems of Galactic Basic"|<ref name="Written" />}}
[[File:Uueg_Tching_Sayings_SWAJ14.png|thumb|left|220px|The ''Sayings'', a collection of Atrisian parables, analogies, and advice, eventually began circulating off-planet.]]
[[Atrisian Emperor (Sayings)|One]] of the emperors of Atrisia eventually ordered the printing of Uueg Tching's ''Sayings'' in a limited run intended for the Atrisian [[Noble/Legends|nobility]]. Furthermore,<ref name="Files" /> around [[539 BBY]],<ref name="539 BBY">{{JournalCite|14|From the Files of Corellia Antilles}}, which is set shortly after the reestablishment of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] following the [[Battle of Onderon (Galactic Civil War)|final defeat]] of the resurrected [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], establishes that the ''[[Sayings]]'' were made available to the general public 550 [[Standard year/Legends|years]] prior. Since ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the former events to [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]], the latter must have occurred around [[539 BBY]].</ref> the [[Atrisian Parliament]], having wrested power from the imperial [[Throne/Legends|throne]], made the ''Sayings'' available in both a specially printed edition and a database format.<ref name="Files" /> Subsequently, both the collection and the Atrisian script it had been written in began to make their way offworld.<ref name="Written" />

Approximately [[39 BBY/Legends|500 years]] later,<ref name="39 BBY">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/88/indexp2.html|text=''Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties''|int=Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties}} establishes that [[Murk Lundi]] researched the history of the [[Atrisian Empire]] at the [[University of Coruscant/Legends|University of Coruscant]] before changing his focus to studying the [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] sect known as the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]]. The first section of ''[[Jedi Apprentice Special Edition: The Followers]]'', the events of which ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates to [[39 BBY/Legends|39 BBY]], depicts Lundi as a researcher of the Sith; therefore the Atrisian Empire must have been a research subject at the University of Coruscant by that [[Time/Legends|time]].</ref> the Atrisian Empire had become a classical field of [[Galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Historian/Legends|historical]] studies at the [[University of Coruscant/Legends|University of Coruscant]].<ref name="Evil Never Dies">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/88/indexp2.html|text=''Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties''|int=Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties}}</ref> In addition, despite space surrounding Atrisia being a part of the territories either unaligned with or contested by the Galactic Republic or the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]] by [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]], the planet fell within the borders of the Republic during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] of [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]]&ndash;[[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].<ref name="TEA" /> During the first campaigns of that conflict, the [[Twentieth Army]] of the [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic Military]] was tasked with defending Atrisia's vicinity against the [[Confederacy military/Legends|military forces]] of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]],<ref name="EGTW" /> and the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]] included the [[Dreadnaught-class heavy cruiser/Legends|''Dreadnaught''-class heavy cruiser]] ''[[Atrisian Iron]]'' by the [[Great ReSynchronization|date]] [[21 BBY/Legends|15:2:29]].<ref name="Insider74">{{InsiderCite|74|CIS Shadowfeed Dispatch 15:2:29 Edition}}</ref>

===Galactic Empire===
{{Quote|Most people associate the Atrisian Empire with exotic danger&mdash;the brutal conquests of its early rulers, the brilliant but ruthless political gambits of Emperor Uueg Tching, the distilled political craftiness of his ''Sayings'', or the sociopathic decadence of the Six Savage Viziers. While the modern Atrisian Commonwealth is a far more mundane place, Atrisian script, the writing system made ubiquitous planetwide by the Kitel Phard Dynasty, has found a place offworld in hands every bit as pitiless as the ancient emperors.|Doctor Milanda Vorgan, "The Written Word: A Brief Introduction to the Writing Systems of Galactic Basic"|<ref name="Written" />}}
[[File:AtrisianCommonwealth-TEA.png|thumb|right|230px|Atrisia and the Atrisian Commonwealth were a part of the Galactic Empire and the New Republic.]]
The Kitel Phard Dynasty of Atrisia served as an inspiration for the formation of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="CSWE Atrisia">{{CSWECite|I|47|Atrisia}}</ref> In his rhetoric addressed at the [[Senator/Legends|senators]] of that newly [[Declaration of a New Order|founded]] regime, [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] promised to bring about a galactic golden age akin to that achieved by the ancient rulers of Atrisia.<ref name="Farlander">{{StoryCite|story=The Farlander Papers|book=Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)}}</ref> By [[17 BBY/Legends|17 BBY]], Atrisia lay within space controlled by the Empire,<ref name="EGTW" /> and certain elements of the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]] were named after aspects of the ancient Atrisian civilization, such as the [[atrisian corps]] of the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]]<ref name="ImperialHandbook">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref> and the military title [[Warlord of the Empire]].<ref name="Warlords">{{SW|url=news/the-imperial-warlords-despoilers-of-an-empire-part-1|series=The Imperial Warlords: Despoilers of an Empire|text=Part 1|nolive=1}}</ref> The planet was mentioned in a [[Holo-brochure|holobrochure]] for the [[Tagge Holographic Museum]] of [[Chandrila/Legends|Chandrila]],<ref name="Creatures" /> and, shortly after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] historian [[Major/Legends|Major]] [[Arhul Hextrophon/Legends|Arhul Hextrophon]] noted the history of Atrisia in a compilation of Imperial documents for Alliance [[Supreme Commander (Alliance)/Legends|Supreme Commander]] [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] and other Rebel [[Officer/Legends|officers]].<ref name="IS2" />

Following the death of Palpatine at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], Atrisia declared its independence from the Empire, and the Atrisian Commonwealth eventually joined the Empire's successor government, the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], as an [[Allied Region]].<ref name="TEA" /> The [[Xenoarchaeology/Legends|xenoarchaeologist]] [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Henrietya Antilles|Corellia Antilles]] mentioned Atrisia in a lecture given at the [[Galactic Museum/Legends|Galactic Museum]] on<ref name="Files" /> the Core Worlds planet [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]<ref name="TEA" /> approximately [[11 ABY/Legends|seven years]] later.<ref name="11 ABY">{{JournalCite|14|From the Files of Corellia Antilles}} is set shortly after the reestablishment of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] following the [[Battle of Onderon (Galactic Civil War)|final defeat]] of the resurrected [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], which ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates to [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]].</ref> In [[38 ABY]], the world was also featured in the [[Xenolinguist/Legends|xenolinguist]] Doctor [[Milanda Vorgan]]'s publication "[[The Written Word: A Brief Introduction to the Writing Systems of Galactic Basic]]." In<ref name="Written" /> her<ref name="TT">{{WEGCite|story=Erasing All Traces|book=The Last Command Sourcebook}}</ref> work, Vorgan noted that most people had since come to associate the ancient Atrisian Empire with exotic danger, especially when compared with the state of the modern Commonwealth.<ref name="Written" /> By [[137 ABY]],<ref name="TEA" /> the ancient planet<ref name="Creatures" /> Atrisia had been incorporated into the [[Core Worlds Security Zone]], an administrative territory of [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire]].<ref name="TEA" />

==Inhabitants==
{{Main|Atrisian}}
{{Quote|An enlightened despot, he ''[Uueg Tching]'' is remembered by Atrisians for his skill in diplomacy, in war, and in maintaining order.|Lecture by Doctor Corellia Antilles|<ref name="Files" />}}
Atrisia was populated by a Human race known as Atrisians, with the population of the Atrisi system around [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]] numbering from 100 million to 500 million.<ref name="TEA" /> Before Tching's Atrisian Empire unified the planet,<ref name="Files" /> Atrisia's continents were inhabited by several nations.<ref name="IS2" /> The Atrisian mythology included [[Wapoe/Legends|Wapoe]], a demigod of disguise.<ref name="CL">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref> Upon the unification of Atrisia by the Kitel Phard Dynasty, the use of the standardized Atrisian script was established planetwide.<ref name="Written" />

[[File:Mohc_Star_Wars_TCG.png|thumb|left|220px|Imperial General Rom Mohc was an Atrisian.]]
Ancient Atrisia was a highly militarized society, and the atrisian corps of the later Galactic Empire was named in honor of the Atrisian warriors of the Kitel Phard Dynasty.<ref name="ImperialHandbook" /> However, the composition of the collection known as ''Sayings'' by Emperor Tching marked a change in Atrisian [[Politics/Legends|politics]] from bloody wars to [[Infiltrator (starfighter)|infiltration]], espionage, and [[Assassin/Legends|assassination]]. Eventually, the Atrisian Parliament took over power formerly held by the imperial throne, but [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]] later, the Atrisians still remembered<ref name="Files" /> the Kitel Phard Dynasty<ref name="IS2" /> and Tching with pride.<ref name="Files" />

Despite eventually achieving interstellar spaceflight, the Atrisians remained an insular culture, although some left their homeworld for the wider galaxy,<ref name="TEA" /> such as [[Rom Mohc]],<ref name="Written" /> who served with the Republic Military during the Clone Wars<ref name="TDFS1">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20050407a|series=The Dark Forces Saga|text=Part 1}}</ref> and eventually became a [[General/Legends|general]] in the Galactic Empire's military forces.<ref name="CSWE Mohc">{{CSWECite|II|323|Mohc, General Rom}}</ref> By the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], there were several noble families of Atrisians, one of which included [[Villis Andal]], who eventually became a [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] of the Galactic Empire.<ref name="Planets">''[[The Star Wars Planets Collection]]''</ref>

==Locations==
{{Quote|The original manuscript of Uueg Tching's ''Sayings'' was kept for the last 3,000 years in the Rare Books Department of the Atrisian Imperial Historical Library on Kitel Phard.|Lecture by Doctor Corellia Antilles|<ref name="Files" />}}
The city of Jar'Kai was located on Atrisia. The Yovshin Swordsmen named swords crafted in that settlement "Jar'Kai," and the name also came to refer to the sword-fighting technique utilizing those weapons.<ref name="TDFS4" /> Atrisia was also the site of the [[Atrisian Imperial Historical Library]]. The original manuscript of Uueg Tching's ''Sayings'' was kept in the [[Rare Books Department]] of the [[Library/Legends|library]]<ref name="CSWE Tching" /> for 3,000 years<ref name="Files" /> before it was transferred to the Imperial Museum on Coruscant<ref name="CSWE Tching" /> around [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]].<ref name="1 BBY">{{JournalCite|14|From the Files of Corellia Antilles}}, which is set shortly after the reestablishment of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] following the [[Battle of Onderon (Galactic Civil War)|final defeat]] of the resurrected [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], establishes that the ''[[Sayings]]'' were transferred to the [[Galactic Museum/Legends|Imperial Museum]] twelve [[Standard year/Legends|years]] prior. Since ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the former events to [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]], the latter must have occurred around [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]].</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Atrisia is from the ''Imperial Sourcebook''; Kitel Phard is from ''Adventure Journal'' #14. Making them one and the same seemed logical&mdash;the ''Imperial Sourcebook'' is clear about the fact that Uueg Tching united a planet. Atrisia's antiquity and apparent importance to galactic culture argued for putting it in the Core Worlds; we stuck it out on the frontier to give it more of a whiff of the exotic and in hopes that future Star Wars creators might find intriguing possibilities in that.|Jason Fry|<ref name="Blog">{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2009/08/endnotes-for-star-wars-essential-atlas_24.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Endnotes for Star Wars: The Essential Atlas (part 2 of 5)}}</ref>}}
[[File:Impsourcebook.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Atrisia was first mentioned in the ''Imperial Sourcebook''.]]
Atrisia was introduced in the ''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]'', a [[1989]] supplement written by [[Greg Gorden]] for [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''. Although the book mentioned "Uueg Tching of Kitel Phard, 54th Emperor of Atrisia," it also introduced the Kitel Phard Dynasty and thus did not definitively establish the nature of the aforementioned "Kitel Phard."<ref name="ISB">''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]''</ref> In [[August]] [[1997]], the article "[[From the Files of Corellia Antilles]]," which was authored by [[Timothy S. O'Brien|Timothy O'Brien]] and published in [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 14|''Star Wars Adventure Journal'' 14]], established that Kitel Phard was an astronomical object.<ref name="Files" /> When writing ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'',<ref name="Blog" /> a reference book by [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Jason Fry]] released in [[2009]],<ref name="TEA" /> co-author Fry felt that it was "logical" to conclude that Atrisia and Kitel Phard referred to the same planet,<ref name="Blog" /> and thus the two were established by the book to be synonyms.<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:Essential_Atlas.jpg|thumb|left|200px|''The Essential Atlas'' provided more contextual information for Atrisia.]]
In addition, due to previously published sources noting Atrisia's antiquity and its cultural importance to the wider galaxy, the authors of ''The Essential Atlas'' decided to place the planet in the Core Worlds region of the galaxy,<ref name="Blog" /> albeit on the very frontier of that region as part of grid square J-12&mdash;near the border of the explored galactic territories.<ref name="TEA" /> This was done intentionally to make Atrisia seem a more exotic location and to provide the authors of future ''[[Star Wars]]'' media with interesting storytelling possibilities.<ref name="Blog" /> "[[Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star, How I Wonder Where We Are]]," a [[1990]] [[roleplaying game]] source article published in [[Voyages SF 13|''Voyages SF'' 13]], had previously placed the Atrisi [[Star system/Legends|system]] in the [[Harron sector/Legends|Harron sector]]. Since the article was released outside of the [[Lucas Licensing]] process, its [[canon]]icity within the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity was never confirmed,<ref name="Twinkle">{{VoyagesCite|13|Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star, How I Wonder Where We Are}}</ref> and ''The Essential Atlas'' overrode the ''Voyages SF'' 13 placement by establishing that the Atrisi system, and therefore Atrisia, was situated outside of the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]]<ref name="TEA" /> in which the Harron sector was later placed.<ref name="Expansion">{{SW|url=news/essential-atlas-extra-expansion-region|text=Essential Atlas Extra: Expansion Region}}</ref>

Atrisia was mentioned in an Underworld Trading Crew Skill mission of the [[2011]] [[BioWare]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', though the information regarding the mission's outcome was later removed from the game.<ref name="Sword Fodder" /> Furthermore, according to an outline for Fry and [[Paul R. Urquhart]]'s [[2012]] reference book, ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'', that book would have detailed the military conflicts taking place on Atrisia. However, the relevant sections, "The Wars of Atrisia" and "World at War: Atrisia," were ultimately not written.<ref name="AuthorCut">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-part-12-tales-of-the-new-republic|series=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|text=Part 12: Tales of the New Republic}}</ref>
